entries.clue: A crab's wandering round beetle (6)

indicatorNotes.wandering round: letters that wander round end up in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A crab scuttles about beside a beetle on the shore.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is surface glue: read 'crab's' as plain letters CRABS and all six are there.
annotation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

entries.clue: I would break up comfort of reinforcement (13)

indicatorNotes.break up: I'D breaks into the other word, splitting it in two

blocks.note: consolation = comfort
I'D is short for I would
container indicator: ID goes inside CONSOL|ATION

annotation.surface: Someone admits they would ruin the comfort that reinforcement brings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break up' looks like an anagram instruction, but here it only means splitting the comfort word in two so the short piece can sit in the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: Consolidation strengthens something, making it firmer: reinforcement.

entries.clue: Mechanism which turns up the same? (7)

indicatorNotes.up the same: in a down entry, read upward it is still the same word

blocks.note: in a down entry, reading 'up' means bottom to top; the word must be a palindrome

annotation.surface: A riddle about a gadget that always turns up looking the same.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turns' does double duty: it describes the mechanism and, with 'up', hints at reading the answer bottom to top in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A rotator is a device that turns something round.

entries.clue: Fortunate there's not so many in cot (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece is placed in the other

blocks.note: a cot is a bed
less = not so many

annotation.surface: A lucky family discovers the cot doesn't hold so many after all.
annotation.walkthrough: A purist would want 'fewer' for 'not so many', but everyday English uses less freely.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'we are blessed with good weather' says the same as 'fortunate to have'.

entries.clue: Wait for old dog, say, to catch cold (6)

indicatorNotes.say: a dog is an example of a pet
indicatorNotes.to catch: to catch something is to hold it, so the dog word takes the cold letter into its middle

blocks.note: ex = former, old
a dog is one kind of pet
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone waits for an elderly dog to come down with a chill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Catch cold' reads as falling ill; split it, and 'catch' is the containment while 'cold' is only its single-letter abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to expect a visitor is to await, or wait for, their arrival.

entries.clue: Head of embassy to send message (5)

indicatorNotes.Head of: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of embassy
to mail is to send by post

annotation.surface: An ambassador is instructed to send a message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Send message' looks like one verb phrase, but the split falls after 'send': MAIL is the verb and 'message' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in modern use: the electronic kind of message, sent over the internet.

entries.clue: Old college opening place of tissue growth (5)

indicatorNotes.opening: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of British college mostly renamed universities in 1992
first letter of place

annotation.surface: An old college opens a site for tissue-growth research.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a verb about the college; it actually picks out the first letter of 'place'.
annotation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small growth of tissue, often on a mucous membrane.

entries.clue: Initial correspondence from London, perhaps (7,6)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: London is just one example of a capital

blocks.note: an initial is the big first letter of a name, as in initials on a monogram
a letter sent from a capital city such as London

annotation.surface: The first letter to arrive from London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initial' reads as an adjective, first, but is the noun: the big letter at the start of a name.
annotation.definitionFit: An initial is the capital letter beginning a name or word.

entries.clue: Curse three articles by mother (8)

indicatorNotes.by: the articles are placed beside mother

blocks.note: AN, A and THE are the three English articles
ma = mother

annotation.surface: Someone swears at three pieces of writing about their mother.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces; here it is grammar, and English has exactly three.
annotation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal curse, especially one pronounced by a church.

entries.clue: Look to gym lesson to make great strides (4)

blocks.note: lo = look, as in 'lo and behold'
PE = physical education, a school gym lesson

annotation.surface: Pupils are told a gym lesson will help them make great strides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make great strides' usually means improve; here it is literal, running with long steps.
annotation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides.

entries.clue: Return implement to get the money (4)

indicatorNotes.Return: to return is to go back, so the word comes back to front

blocks.note: a tool is an implement
reversal indicator

annotation.surface: Someone hands back a tool in exchange for cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return' reads as handing the implement back; it means writing it back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: besides plunder, the word is everyday slang for cash.

entries.clue: Tipsy elf, drunk with negative emotion (4-4)

indicatorNotes.drunk: drunk letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A tipsy elf, now properly drunk, turns maudlin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tipsy' sits beside 'drunk' as if both describe the elf; 'tipsy' is fodder and only 'drunk' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: wallowing in sorrow for one's own troubles is one of many negative emotions.

entries.clue: Draw colour in rows (6)

blocks.note: a draw in a match is a tie
red is a colour

annotation.surface: An artist is told to draw and colour in rows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' and 'colour' read as art-class verbs; both are nouns here, a drawn game and a shade.
annotation.definitionFit: Something tiered is arranged in rows or layers, one above another.

entries.clue: Side of the head where prayers are heard (6)

blocks.note: the flat area between eye and ear
a building for worship

annotation.surface: A picture of prayers heard right beside one's head.
annotation.walkthrough: The joins are seamless: 'heard' tempts you towards the ear and a homophone, but both halves are plain definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: The temple is both the side of the forehead and a building for worship.

entries.clue: Little child sheltering close this evening (7)

indicatorNotes.sheltering: the child shelters the other word inside it

blocks.note: a tot is a little child
nigh = close, near

annotation.surface: A small child is taken in as night draws close.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb, as in shutting up for the evening; it is the adjective meaning near, in its old-fashioned form.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'see you tonight' and 'see you this evening' mean the same.

entries.clue: Club concealing the broken knife (7)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the club hides the other letters inside it

blocks.note: a mace is a heavy club
THE rearranged

annotation.surface: A club hides a broken knife in a crime-scene picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broken' seems to describe the knife, but it is the word 'the' that gets broken before the club hides it, one letter from its end.
annotation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad, heavy knife used for cutting vegetation.

entries.clue: Orange tongue? (8)

blocks.note: the fruit, not the colour: a small, loose-skinned citrus
tongue = language; here the main one spoken in China

annotation.surface: An orange tongue, as after too many sweets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Orange' reads as a colour and 'tongue' as the body part; the fruit and the language are meant.
annotation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a citrus fruit, and Mandarin is a Chinese language, a tongue.

entries.clue: Fear concerning father being on the outside (5)

indicatorNotes.being on the outside: father sits outside the other word, wrapping it

blocks.note: dad = father
re = concerning, as in memo headers

annotation.surface: A child worries about their father being outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like an adjective meaning worrying, which suits the surface; it is the preposition, as in 'about'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, noun for noun: dread is fear of something to come, often heavy and anticipatory.

entries.clue: Show noisy commentary (5)

indicatorNotes.noisy: a noisy word is one heard rather than read

blocks.note: a review is a critical commentary

annotation.surface: A show accompanied by a loud commentator.
annotation.walkthrough: REVIEW and REVUE are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A revue is a stage show of sketches, songs and dances.

entries.clue: Almost split symbol when scoring (4)

indicatorNotes.Almost: almost the whole word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: CLEFT (split) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A sports report on a symbol that nearly divides the scorers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' suggests goals; it means writing a musical score.
annotation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a stave fixing the pitch of the notes, used when writing music.

entries.clue: Queue for something to say (4)

blocks.note: people waiting one behind another, as Americans say it
a piece of an actor's script

annotation.surface: Someone joins a queue just to have something to talk about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queue' reads as a verb, but it is the noun; 'for' just links the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: A line is both a queue of people and a scripted piece of speech.

entries.clue: Give tent away in brief scene (8)

indicatorNotes.away: letters sent away scatter into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Handing over a tent in a short scene of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give away' reads as one phrasal verb; 'give' is fodder and 'away' alone is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A vignette is a short descriptive scene or sketch.

entries.clue: Nervous near the brink? (2,4)

blocks.note: tense and jumpy, the idiomatic sense
the literal sense: positioned right at the rim

annotation.surface: Someone standing near a cliff edge is understandably nervous.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is the idiom taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: On edge means tense and nervous, and literally sitting at an edge.

entries.clue: Supposition on the old railway (6)

blocks.note: used as it stands
O = old, a standard abbreviation
RY = railway, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A hunch about a disused railway line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is just a link here, as in a theory on the subject; RY is the old abbreviation seen in railway company names.
annotation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition put forward to explain something.
